stories.h: INEC sets 28 November mock accreditation to test new election safeguards
stories.e: The Independent National Electoral Commission has scheduled a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise for 28 November to test an upgraded Bimodal Voter Accreditation System ahead of the 2027 general election. Chairman Joash Amupitan, speaking in London, said the commission has introduced a safeguard that blocks inaccurate polling-unit results from reaching its result-viewing portal, and has cut the maximum number of voters assigned to each device from 1,250 to 850.

stories.h: INEC sets 28 November for nationwide mock accreditation ahead of 2027 polls
stories.e: The Independent National Electoral Commission has scheduled a nationwide mock accreditation exercise for 28 November to field-test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and other equipment before the February 2027 general election. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan said the exercise would help identify technical gaps, though the plan's scope has been constrained by budget limits.

stories.h: Court commits Maina's son to begin serving seven-year jail term
stories.e: A Nigerian court has ordered Faisal Maina, son of former pension reform taskforce chairman Abdulrasheed Maina, to be committed to prison to begin serving a seven-year sentence over the multi-billion-naira pension fraud scandal. The term follows an earlier appellate ruling that had halved his original 14-year sentence.

stories.h: EFCC arraigns businessman over alleged £122,000 investment fraud
stories.e: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission arraigned businessman Ashley Oshin before a Lagos State High Court over an alleged £122,000 investment fraud dating back to 2009. He is accused of promising two investors a 40 per cent annual return through a fund he knew to be fraudulent, and he pleaded not guilty. The judge remanded him in a correctional centre and adjourned the matter to 18 November for trial and a bail hearing.

stories.h: FIJ journalist Daniel Ojukwu remanded in Kuje over SDG spending investigation
stories.e: A Federal High Court in Abuja remanded investigative journalist Daniel Ojukwu in Kuje Correctional Centre after he pleaded not guilty to 12 counts of cyberstalking and criminal defamation linked to his reporting on spending by the presidential SDG office. The case stems from Foundation for Investigative Journalism reports that questioned how funds were used under former aide Adejoke Orelope-Adefulire. His bail hearing was adjourned to 1 December, while press-freedom groups have condemned the prosecution as an attempt to intimidate reporters covering public spending.

stories.h: Makinde campaign group demands probe of Tinubu's ₦11.2trn crude-backed loans
stories.e: A campaign organisation backing Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde's presidential bid has called for an open investigation into federal plans to pledge about 340 million barrels of future crude output to secure roughly ₦11.2 trillion in loans. The group wants the government to disclose the lenders, interest rates, fees and repayment terms behind four financing arrangements, warning that mortgaging future oil revenue could leave Nigeria worse off if prices rise. It has urged the National Assembly to hold a public hearing and President Tinubu to explain the deals.

stories.h: EFCC witness alleges Emefiele used associates to acquire properties
stories.e: An investigator testifying for the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission told a Nigerian court that former Central Bank governor Godwin Emefiele used associates to acquire properties in Lagos, Delta, Ogun and Abuja states, as part of the ongoing corruption trial against him. The testimony adds to the EFCC's long-running effort to trace and recover assets allegedly linked to Emefiele since his 2023 arrest.

stories.h: Court jails Mainas son for seven years over pension fraud laundering
stories.e: The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered that Faisal Maina, son of jailed former pension boss Abdulrasheed Maina, be moved to a correctional centre to serve a seven-year sentence. Justice James Omotosho granted an EFCC application to enforce the conviction after Maina fled trial in 2020 and was later re-arrested in Abuja in October. He was convicted in 2021 of laundering over N58 million in pension funds through a fictitious bank account.

stories.h: INEC says fake AI-generated photos found in voter register across 10 states
stories.e: Nigeria's electoral commission disclosed that officials in ten states had uploaded AI-generated images into the national voters' register, which have since been pulled down. INEC Commissioner Mohammed Kudu Haruna said the implicated staff have been identified and face disciplinary action, as the commission races to finalise an artificial-intelligence policy ahead of the 2027 polls. The episode has added to concerns over the integrity of the preliminary voter register.

stories.h: Osun offices shut as workers begin three-day strike over withheld council funds
stories.e: Government offices across Osun State closed on Monday as the state chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress began a three-day solidarity strike with local government workers, after a seven-day ultimatum over withheld council allocations expired. The dispute forms part of a long-running row between the state and federal authorities over control of local government funds, which the Supreme Court weighed in on in December 2025. Public services in the state were disrupted as the action took effect.

stories.h: ICPC adds four civil servants as co-defendants in fake PFIPC agency case
stories.e: The Independent Corrupt Practices Commission has amended its charges against Adeniyi Adeyemi, accused of running the non-existent Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council, raising the count from 22 to 36 and naming four federal civil servants as co-defendants. The FCT High Court in Abuja adjourned the case to 18 November after one of the new defendants was absent on health grounds. Prosecutors allege the civil servants helped the fake agency secure budgetary allocation and official recognition.

stories.h: SERAP demands disclosure of ₦50,000 relief payment beneficiaries from Doro's ministry
stories.e: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project has written to the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Bernard Doro, demanding full disclosure of how beneficiaries of the ₦50,000 National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention are selected, paid and monitored. The group wants the EFCC and ICPC invited to oversee the scheme and says some intended recipients have reported being unable to access funds or being wrongly deemed ineligible.

stories.h: Kogi state withholds details of ₦7bn primary healthcare upgrade as clinics found incomplete
stories.e: Kogi State says it has committed over ₦7 billion, backed by World Bank funding, to upgrade 88 primary healthcare centres, but has refused to release the full list of facilities or supporting inspection and completion records despite a Freedom of Information request. Premium Times visited several of the listed clinics and found some locked and unstaffed, others lacking water or power, and one still operating out of borrowed classrooms years after flood damage.

stories.h: Delta State to spend over N2billion sponsoring pilgrims despite residents economic hardship
stories.e: Delta States government has committed more than N2 billion to fully sponsor Christian pilgrims travelling to Israel and Jordan this year, with successful applicants also receiving extra allowances for gifts and religious items. The spending comes as the state carries a debt burden exceeding N369 billion and as civil society groups estimate that around 1.5 million residents live in multidimensional poverty, prompting questions about spending priorities.

stories.h: EFCC says Ogun refinery clampdown also uncovered illegal alcohol production and mining
stories.e: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission says its continuing operation against an illegal refinery site in Ogun State has also turned up evidence of illicit alcohol production and unauthorised mining activity in the area. The disclosure follows the Commission's earlier arrests over suspected illegal lithium processing and a separate suspected illegal refinery found deserted nearby.

stories.h: NNPC denies its gas supply is behind Nigeria's power generation slump
stories.e: NNPC Limited has pushed back against suggestions that bottlenecks in its gas transport network are responsible for the recent drop in electricity generation across Lagos, Abuja and other major cities. The company said its gas infrastructure subsidiary shows no transport-related shortfalls, and called for grid operator NISO and other industry players to jointly review the data behind the outages rather than single out gas supply.

stories.h: Obi demands Tinubu account for ₦15.8trn subsidy savings and foreign loans
stories.e: Peter Obi has publicly challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain how the Federal Government has spent the ₦15.8 trillion in fuel subsidy savings and more than $100 billion in new borrowing accumulated since 2023. The ADC chieftain framed the request as a direct test of transparency ahead of the 2027 elections, arguing that ordinary Nigerians deserve a full account of where these resources have gone.

stories.h: Delta State to spend over ₦2bn sponsoring Christian pilgrims to Israel and Jordan
stories.e: Delta State has announced it will spend more than ₦2 billion fully sponsoring successful applicants for the 2026 Christian pilgrimage to Israel and Jordan, with screening by the Nigeria Christian Pilgrim Commission starting in Asaba from 11 November. The announcement comes as the state carries about ₦369.3 billion in debt, and advocacy group ANEEJ has previously estimated that 1.5 million Deltans live in multidimensional poverty. Officials describe the programme as spiritual renewal and part of a broader human development strategy.

stories.h: Osun's local councils received ₦238.4bn in 18 months, but where did it go?
stories.e: Analysis of federal allocation data shows Osun's 30 local government areas received about ₦238.4 billion between January 2025 and June 2026, even as residents complain of poor roads, understaffed clinics and broken water systems. The state's Auditor-General for Local Governments says he cannot audit the funds because the Central Bank of Nigeria has not supplied the bank statements he requested, amid a wider dispute between APC- and PDP-aligned council leaders over control of local government accounts. A BudgIT review separately found most monitored health centres and several school projects fell short of basic standards.

stories.h: Retiring Supreme Court justice says some colleagues remain under a US travel ban
stories.e: At her valedictory session in Abuja, retiring Justice Uwani Musa Abba-Aji said some Supreme Court justices still face US travel restrictions linked to a widely criticised judgment, which she said was misinterpreted. The restrictions are commonly tied to the seven-judge panel's January 2020 ruling that overturned Emeka Ihedioha's Imo State governorship win in favour of Hope Uzodimma. Neither the US government nor the Supreme Court has publicly commented on the claim.

stories.h: INEC chairman Amupitan says his loyalty is solely to the constitution
stories.e: Facing renewed criticism over the commission's handling of pre-2027 election disputes, INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan said his allegiance is to the constitution and the will of Nigerians, not to any political interest. The remarks come amid opposition pressure over INEC's rulings on party primaries and candidate lists ahead of next year's polls.

stories.h: Federal High Court orders INEC to list Adebutu as Ogun PDP governorship candidate
stories.e: Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered INEC to publish Ladi Adebutu's name as the PDP's governorship candidate for Ogun State within 24 hours, ruling that the commission had no power to exclude a candidate properly nominated by his party. INEC had dropped Adebutu over an alleged register dispute, but the court found the party had complied with submission rules.

stories.h: Senate committee warns petroleum regulators against sabotaging government policy
stories.e: The Senate Committee on Petroleum Downstream, chaired by Kawu Sumaila, warned regulatory agencies in the oil and gas sector against undermining government policy, saying some agencies were failing to support the president's vision for the sector. The warning came as the committee cleared seven nominees for executive director roles at the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority.

stories.h: 2027 Politics Watch: political violence flares as ADC suffers legal setback
stories.e: A Premium Times politics roundup highlights rising political violence ahead of the 2027 elections alongside an internal legal setback for the opposition African Democratic Congress. The report forms part of ongoing coverage tracking party manoeuvring and unrest as campaigning for the 2027 polls intensifies.

stories.h: Federal government reviews 932 laws, scraps 269 obsolete enactments
stories.e: The federal government has completed a review of 932 existing laws and removed 269 obsolete enactments from the new Laws of the Federation of Nigeria. The exercise is intended to modernise the statute book and strip out redundant or conflicting legislation.

stories.h: INEC adds safeguard to block inaccurate results from IReV, sets mock poll for 28 November
stories.e: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan said the commission has built a technical safeguard that will stop inaccurate polling-unit results from reaching its public result-viewing portal, aiming to close gaps exposed during the 2023 elections. He announced that a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise will take place on 28 November to test the upgraded system before the 2027 general elections. The presidential and National Assembly polls are scheduled for 16 January 2027, with governorship elections to follow in February.

stories.h: Dickson alleges plot to rig 2027 polls using fake security officers
stories.e: Nigeria Democratic Congress leader and Bayelsa West senator Seriake Dickson has alleged, in remarks to party youth and women leaders in Bayelsa State, that there are plans to manipulate the 2027 election and intimidate voters using impersonated security personnel. He urged INEC and security agencies to act impartially and called on supporters to resist any malpractice through lawful means rather than confrontation.

stories.h: Makinde explains decision to challenge Tinubu in 2027 presidential race
stories.e: Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, now the Allied Peoples Movement's presidential candidate, has published a newsletter explaining why he withdrew his backing for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the January 2027 election. He argues the government has stabilised the economy without translating the gains into jobs or living standards, and faults its handling of fuel subsidy removal and the weakening of opposition parties. Makinde says he would serve a single four-year term leading a transitional government of national unity.

stories.h: Thugs disrupt Peter Obis NDC town hall meeting in Lagos
stories.e: A town hall event for NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi in Lagos was disrupted when suspected thugs attacked attendees, damaging property and injuring some participants, according to eyewitnesses. The incident adds to a string of violent disruptions at opposition political gatherings ahead of the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Ruling APC pledges 8% inflation target and 7,500MW power generation in Tinubu re-election plan
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu's All Progressives Congress has unveiled campaign pledges for a prospective second term, promising to cut inflation to 8 per cent or below and raise average peak electricity generation to 7,500 megawatts. The plan also proposes expanding food storage and processing capacity to curb post-harvest losses. The pledges arrive as headline inflation, in double digits since 2023, eased to 14.63 per cent in September 2026.

stories.h: Saraki accuses Kwara government of abusing prosecutorial powers as Offa robbery charges are cut
stories.e: Former Senate President Bukola Saraki has accused the Kwara State Government of abusing its prosecutorial powers after it withdrew 18 of the 20 charges filed against him and former governor Abdulfatah Ahmed over the 2018 Offa bank robbery. His reaction came after a former ruling-party figure admitted helping to link Saraki to the robbery to settle political scores. Two charges, relating to alleged gang membership and concealment of a vehicle, remain, and Saraki's lawyers say they will contest them in court.

stories.h: Armed thugs attack NDC rally in Asaba, one reported dead
stories.e: Suspected thugs attacked a march by supporters of the opposition NDC's Obidient/OK Movement in Asaba, Delta State, over the weekend, damaging more than thirty vehicles and injuring over ten people, with police confirming one death. Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege condemned the assault as politically motivated and demanded a full investigation, while the Delta State Government and the ruling APC also called the attack unacceptable.

stories.h: Court nullifies ADC leadership, voids Atiku's 2027 presidential ticket
stories.e: A Federal High Court judge in Abuja has nullified the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress and voided the party primary that selected Atiku Abubakar as its 2027 presidential candidate, finding the leadership breached the party's own constitution and electoral law. INEC says it cannot take a position until it receives the certified judgment and will deliberate at its next meeting, while the ADC has lodged an appeal seeking a stay of execution.

stories.h: Lagos police ask political parties to notify command before 2027 rallies
stories.e: Lagos's police commissioner has asked political parties to formally notify the command ahead of rallies, processions and other campaign gatherings as the 2027 election cycle gets under way, saying advance notice lets officers plan security and protect all parties equally. He stressed the request is not a bid for permission, since the Electoral Act obliges police to secure lawful political gatherings, but warned that organisers who ignore agreed security arrangements and cause a breach of the peace will be held responsible.

stories.h: Nigerian Air Force redeploys 67 senior officers in major reshuffle
stories.e: The Nigerian Air Force has reassigned 67 Air Vice Marshals to new posts across its headquarters, operational commands, training institutions and the Defence Headquarters, including a new commander for Operation Hadin Kai, the joint task force fighting Boko Haram and ISWAP in the north-east. The service said the exercise, approved by the Chief of the Air Staff, is meant to match officers' skills to its current operational priorities, with affected officers given until 13 November to complete handover.

stories.h: One killed, five injured as violence disrupts NDC rally in Asaba
stories.e: Delta State Police confirmed one death and five injuries after violence broke out during a Saturday rally organised by supporters of NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi along Nnebisi Road in Asaba. Police said they had warned organisers against staging a road procession after receiving intelligence of possible trouble, and the state commissioner of police has ordered an investigation while condemning the clash.

stories.h: Kwankwaso says he regrets not partnering with Obi ahead of the 2023 election
stories.e: Nigeria Democratic Congress vice-presidential candidate Rabiu Kwankwaso told supporters in Dutse that he now regrets turning down an alliance with Peter Obi before the 2023 presidential election, saying their combined ticket could have defeated the ruling party. He had previously run separately under the NNPP, finishing fourth, while Obi came third, and he linked the admission to their current 2027 partnership.

stories.h: Makinde tells Nigerians to take politicians' money but vote their conscience
stories.e: Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement presidential candidate Seyi Makinde urged supporters at a 2027 campaign event in Bauchi to accept cash handouts from politicians but still vote according to their own judgement. He presented his proposed Reset Agenda as a response to hunger, insecurity and political exclusion, while his host, Bauchi Governor Bala Mohammed, pressed for fairer federal appointments for the region.

stories.h: OK Movement demands probe after armed hoodlums attack NDC march in Asaba
stories.e: The Obi/Kwankwaso Movement's Delta State coordinator, Favour Emerue, has demanded an immediate and transparent investigation after armed hoodlums allegedly attacked NDC supporters taking part in a One Million Man March in Asaba, injuring several and vandalising campaign vehicles. The group is calling on Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and federal security agencies to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible, including any sponsors.

stories.h: Makinde urges supporters to take vote-buying cash but vote their conscience
stories.e: Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde told supporters at a political gathering that they should feel free to accept money offered by vote buyers, but should ultimately cast their ballots according to their own conscience rather than in exchange for cash. The remarks, made ahead of the 2027 general election, have reignited debate about Nigerias entrenched vote-buying culture and its effect on electoral integrity.

stories.h: Deutsche Bank arranges $516m financing for Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway
stories.e: Deutsche Bank has secured $516.3 million in Shariah-compliant financing, backed by an ICIEC sovereign insurance policy, to fund the first phase of Nigeria's planned 1,290km Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway. The nine-year facility covers only the opening section of the route, with the rest of the project still to be financed.

stories.h: FG signs Port Harcourt airport concession deal, pledges to protect workers
stories.e: The Federal Government has formally signed the concession agreement handing Port Harcourt International Airport to a private operator, following a similar deal earlier this year for Enugu's Akanu Ibiam Airport. Officials pledged to safeguard the interests of existing aviation workers, after unions had warned the concession could put jobs at risk.

stories.h: FG concessions Port Harcourt airport, assures workers of job security
stories.e: The federal government has handed Port Harcourt International Airport to a private concessionaire as part of its airport privatisation drive, while assuring existing staff that their jobs will be protected under the new arrangement. The move forms part of a wider push to improve infrastructure and efficiency at airports across the country.

stories.h: Staple food prices surge in Lagos markets, signalling fresh rise in food inflation
stories.e: A BusinessDay survey of Lagos's Mile 12 and Ketu markets found sharp October price rises for staples such as onions, maize and rice, with a 100kg bag of onions nearly quadrupling in price. Traders blamed higher transport and fuel costs, tight supply and festive-season stockpiling, while analysts expect the trend to push food inflation higher after September's rate of 19.59 per cent. The increases add to pressure on households already grappling with a high cost of living.

stories.h: Dangote refinery IPO falls short of 10-million-investor target despite N6.4trn in demand
stories.e: Aliko Dangote has confirmed that the public offer for shares in Dangote Petroleum Refinery fell short of its goal of attracting 10 million individual investors, even though subscription orders reached roughly N6.4 trillion, nearly three times the value on offer. He attributed the shortfall to the limited subscription window and access difficulties faced by some prospective investors. The mismatch between strong demand value and weak investor-number turnout has drawn scrutiny of the offer's retail outreach.

stories.h: Tinubu urges focus on production as Lagos Trade Fair opens
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu, represented by Minister of State for Industry John Enoh, told exhibitors from more than twenty countries at the opening of the 40th Lagos International Trade Fair that his government's reforms have stabilised the economy and that attention must now turn to production, jobs and manufacturing. He cited external reserves reaching about $55 billion in October and inflation easing to 14.63 per cent in September, and announced Nigeria will host the Intra-African Trade Fair for the first time in 2027.

stories.h: Nigeria among six African countries holding 80% of continent's corporate debt – OECD
stories.e: An OECD report finds that Nigeria is one of six African countries that together account for roughly 80 per cent of the continent's corporate debt. The finding highlights how concentrated corporate borrowing remains among a handful of larger African economies even as financing needs grow continent-wide.

stories.h: Nigeria's CNG stations reach 160 as private investment hits $2.6bn, says official
stories.e: The head of the Presidential Compressed Natural Gas Initiative says Nigeria now has about 160 operational CNG refuelling stations, with roughly 170 more in development, after attracting close to $2.6 billion in private investment in under two years. Speaking at the commissioning of a new station in Abuja, officials said the scheme aims to cut transport costs for commuters following the 2023 removal of the petrol subsidy.

stories.h: Nigeria's external debt climbs 6.6% to $145bn in 2025, World Bank reports
stories.e: The World Bank's International Debt Report 2026 puts Nigeria's external debt stock at about $145 billion in 2025, a 6.6 per cent rise from the previous year and a 74 per cent jump since 2015, with private and short-term obligations making up more than half the total. The report shows debt service absorbing 19 per cent of export earnings, and notes multilateral lenders, led by the World Bank's IDA, as Nigeria's biggest creditor group. It comes as developing countries' combined external debt hit a record $9.4 trillion in 2025.

stories.h: Nigeria posts Africa's largest dollar GDP gain, IMF data shows
stories.e: New IMF estimates show Nigeria's economy grew in dollar terms from $290.5 billion to $386.7 billion over the past year, the biggest absolute increase of any African country, helped largely by a stronger naira. Nigeria nonetheless remains Africa's third-largest economy behind South Africa and Egypt, and analysts note the IMF's 4.2 per cent 2026 growth forecast still lags faster-growing peers such as Ethiopia.

stories.h: Delta leads states in latest FAAC allocations as Lagos slips to fifth
stories.e: Nigeria's 36 states shared a combined ₦1.07 trillion in net FAAC allocations for August revenue, with Delta topping the table at ₦98.27 billion on the strength of oil derivation payments. Lagos, long the top earner from VAT, fell to fifth place as its growth lagged other states and deductions for debt and VAT adjustments cut into its take. The top ten states, mostly oil producers, cornered nearly half of all disbursements, underscoring how derivation revenue continues to concentrate public funds among a few states.

stories.h: Dangote Cement-led selloff wipes N3.28trn off Nigerian stock market in a day
stories.e: The Nigerian Exchange shed N3.28 trillion in value on Thursday as Dangote Cement alone lost a tenth of its share price, dragging the All-Share Index below the 250,000-point mark. Presco and UACN also posted double-digit and near double-digit declines, ending a year of strong gains on a sharply negative note.

stories.h: Nigeria's External Debt Hits $145bn as Servicing Burden Rises, World Bank Says
stories.e: A new World Bank assessment finds Nigeria's external debt has climbed to roughly $145 billion, with the cost of servicing that debt rising as a share of government spending. The report adds to concerns from economists and lawmakers about the sustainability of Nigeria's borrowing path ahead of planned fresh loans to fund the 2026 budget.

stories.h: Cooking gas to cost more as Dangote Refinery raises LPG gantry price to N1,000/kg
stories.e: Dangote Refinery lifted its LPG gantry price by 8.1% to N1,000 per kilogram, even as Lagos depots were already selling at N1,450/kg. Industry players warn the increase could stall Nigeria's shift away from firewood and kerosene toward cleaner cooking gas, despite a 17.78% year-on-year rise in domestic LPG supply.

stories.h: Finance Minister Says E-Invoicing Helped Push Nigeria's Revenue to N33 Trillion in 10 Months
stories.e: Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele says Nigeria collected a record N33 trillion in government revenue between January and October 2026, crediting digital tools like e-invoicing for improving tax collection. He argued that Nigeria's data should be treated as a strategic national asset, noting that most of the country's data is currently hosted on servers outside Nigeria.

stories.h: Grid operator blames gas shortages, low water levels for Nigeria's power slump
stories.e: The Nigerian Independent System Operator says tight gas supply to thermal plants and reduced water inflows at the Kainji, Jebba and Shiroro hydro stations have cut electricity generation nationwide, forcing longer outages for distribution companies. NISO gave no timeline for recovery, leaving households and businesses more reliant on generators and solar.

stories.h: Nigeria's port exports up 25% in two years, NPA tells World Ports Conference
stories.e: NPA managing director Abubakar Dantsoho told the World Ports Conference in London that Nigerian exports have grown more than 25% over two years, driven by manufacturing and agriculture as well as oil. He pointed to new export-processing terminals and a planned $1 billion Apapa Port upgrade as further boosts to trade capacity.

stories.h: NESG: Power shortages, credit squeeze slow Nigeria's business activity in October
stories.e: The Nigerian Economic Summit Group's October Business Confidence Monitor found firms citing unreliable electricity, tight access to credit, insecurity and high rents as the biggest drags on operations, even as its headline performance index eased slightly from September. Manufacturers reported outages and raw-material shortages while agribusinesses pointed to financing gaps and energy shortfalls, though expectations for coming months improved.

stories.h: NNPC remittance to federal government slips to N11.14trn in nine months
stories.e: NNPC's latest report shows it remitted N11.14 trillion to the federal government between January and September 2026, slightly down from the same period a year earlier despite higher crude and gas production. The figures also show petrol availability at NNPC's own retail stations falling sharply, even as the company points to progress on major gas pipeline projects.

stories.h: AFD signs $60m loan deals with Bank of Industry, Sterling Bank to support Nigerian businesses
stories.e: France's development agency, AFD, has signed loan agreements worth a combined $60 million with the Bank of Industry and Sterling Bank to boost financing for Nigerian businesses, including a $30 million facility earmarked for the country's cultural and creative industries. The deals aim to widen access to affordable credit for Nigerian firms.

stories.h: Nigerian banks earn N522bn from electronic banking and card fees in 9M 2026
stories.e: Nigeria's banks collectively generated N522 billion in income from electronic banking services and card-related fees in the first nine months of 2026. The figure highlights how digital transaction charges have become an increasingly significant revenue stream for lenders.

stories.h: S&P says Nigeria's 2029 investment-grade target may be too ambitious
stories.e: S&P Global Ratings has cast doubt on Nigeria's target of regaining investment-grade credit status by 2029, saying no sovereign has historically moved from a single-B rating to investment grade within just three years. An S&P research director for Africa said sustained reform matters more than hitting a fixed timeline, even while acknowledging recent progress that led to Nigeria's first ratings upgrade since 2012.

stories.h: Naira slides to N1,445/$ in parallel market as gap with official rate widens
stories.e: The naira weakened to N1,445 to the dollar in the parallel market, widening the gap with the official exchange rate to N86.50. The depreciation highlights continuing pressure on the currency despite the Central Bank's recent efforts to narrow the spread between the two markets.

stories.h: Investors pour ₦1.08trn into 364-day treasury bill, nearly doubling target offer
stories.e: Nigerian investors subscribed ₦1.08 trillion to the latest 364-day Nigerian Treasury Bill auction, about 180 per cent of the ₦600 billion the government had offered. The strong demand reflects continued investor appetite for short-term government debt amid high interest rates and a cautious lending environment among commercial banks. The result mirrors a wider pattern in which savers and institutions have favoured government securities over riskier assets this year.

stories.h: Banks' ₦55.7trn loan book grows slowly despite recapitalisation drive
stories.e: Loans and advances at eight major Nigerian banks rose by only 2.4 per cent to ₦55.66 trillion in the nine months to September, even after the industry's recapitalisation exercise raised a combined ₦4.65 trillion. Analysts say lenders remain cautious about extending credit in a high interest-rate environment and continue to favour government securities over loans to businesses. Customer deposits grew faster than lending, pushing the industry's loan-to-deposit ratio down to about 37.2 per cent.

stories.h: Naira suffers biggest single-day loss since October as it slips to N1,364/$
stories.e: The naira closed at N1,364 to the dollar on the official market on 11 November, down from N1,353.50 the previous session in its steepest single-day fall since 22 October, a 0.78 per cent depreciation. The currency remains stronger than its N1,431/$ close at the start of 2026, though foreign reserves grew by just $295.35 million in October, the slowest monthly gain this year. The parallel market quoted the naira even weaker, at around N1,430/$.

stories.h: Naira forecast to stay below N1,400/$ through the festive season
stories.e: Analysts expect the naira to continue trading between N1,290 and N1,400 to the dollar through the rest of the year, supported by stronger foreign reserves, diaspora remittances and steady crude output. The currency has recently held near N1,350 on the official market. Forecasters caution that seasonal festive demand for foreign exchange and a persistent parallel-market premium could still add pressure on the local currency.

stories.h: Access Holdings weighs exit from foreign unit to meet CBN's capital rules
stories.e: Access Holdings is considering divesting from at least one underperforming foreign subsidiary as it works to bring its overseas equity investments within the Central Bank of Nigeria's 10 per cent capital limit. The group is also pursuing capital repatriation and minority stake sales across its banking arm, which held 19.4 per cent of shareholders' funds in foreign investments as of May. The bank is working towards meeting the requirement ahead of a March deadline.

stories.h: Dangote refinery share sale falls short of 10 million investor target
stories.e: Aliko Dangote has acknowledged that his refinerys record-breaking initial public offering fell short of its ambitious goal of attracting 10 million Nigerian retail investors, though the company has yet to release an official final subscriber count. Dangote attributed the shortfall partly to the limited subscription window and to many potential investors not knowing how to participate, while comparing the turnout favourably with past Nigerian and African share offers.

stories.h: Naira weakens 0.22% as forex turnover slows in November's first week
stories.e: The naira slipped against the dollar in the first week of November as foreign exchange turnover on the official market slowed to about $1.45 billion, according to an analysis of Central Bank data. The report notes the currency has now extended its losses for a second consecutive week, continuing a trend flagged in separate CBN research on Nigeria's wider external deficit.

stories.h: Banks park ₦8.31trn at CBN even as apex bank mops up ₦724bn via OMO
stories.e: Nigerian banks held a record ₦8.31 trillion in the Central Bank's Standing Deposit Facility as of 6 November, up nearly 20 per cent in just two days, despite the CBN draining ₦724.32 billion through an Open Market Operations auction. Analysts say the gap shows banking-system liquidity remains unusually high ahead of further OMO auctions and November's Monetary Policy Committee meeting.

stories.h: OPay's withdrawn $304m US listing raises questions about oversight, commentary argues
stories.e: OPay pulled its planned $304 million US share sale in late October, a day after pricing shares that would have valued the fintech near $4 billion, citing an undisclosed regulatory inquiry abroad that it called unrelated to its Nigerian business. A ThisDay commentary argues the episode should push Nigerian regulators, including the CBN and NDIC, to tighten scrutiny of complex corporate structures, digital lending practices and how customer savings are protected. It calls on OPay to keep Nigerian authorities informed despite the company's complex international ownership structure.

stories.h: Nigerian stock investors lose ₦3.52trn in five-day market slump
stories.e: Nigerian equity investors lost about ₦3.52 trillion over the week ending 6 November as profit-taking hit heavyweight stocks including Dangote Cement, Aradel Holdings and HBM Nigeria, pulling the NGX All-Share Index down 2.13 per cent. Analysts attributed the sell-off to investors locking in gains after recent rallies, even as some stocks such as Honeywell Flour Mills and Champion Breweries posted strong gains. The banking and industrial goods sectors were among the hardest hit for the week.

stories.h: CBN sets N15bn minimum capital for foreign stablecoin issuers operating in Nigeria
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria has fixed a N15 billion minimum paid-up capital requirement for issuers of foreign currency-referenced stablecoins, higher than the N10 billion required for naira-pegged tokens. Foreign issuers serving Nigerian users must now incorporate locally and maintain a licensed, staffed presence in the country, with no offshore exemptions allowed.

stories.h: CBN's 2027 Data Localisation Deadline Puts Banks, Fintechs Under Pressure
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria has set a January 2027 deadline for banks, fintechs and mobile money operators to store Nigerian payment data on local servers, a rule officials say will strengthen oversight of the financial system. Industry players warn that smaller players may struggle to comply, with a recent survey finding only about 59% of institutions ready to meet the deadline.

stories.h: Developing Countries' External Debt Hits Record $9.4 Trillion in 2025 - World Bank
stories.e: The World Bank reported that external debt owed by developing countries, including Nigeria, climbed to an unprecedented $9.4 trillion in 2025, a 5.5% jump marking the fastest growth pace since 2021. The report found the poorest nations are now paying the highest borrowing costs in decades, leaving governments less room to fund long-term development.

stories.h: CBN mops up N3.46trn in OMO and treasury bill auctions, holds stop rates steady
stories.e: The CBN allotted about N3.46 trillion combined across its latest OMO and treasury bills auctions, drawing bids worth N5.57 trillion against a much smaller offer. Stop rates on both instruments were left unchanged, with the 364-day treasury bill again attracting the heaviest demand ahead of this month's Monetary Policy Committee meeting.

stories.h: NGX sheds N3.28trn in a day as Dangote Cement, Presco and top banks slide
stories.e: Nigeria's stock market lost N3.28 trillion in value on November 5 as heavy selling hit Dangote Cement, Presco, UACN and several Tier 1 banks, with Dangote Cement's drop alone wiping out roughly N2.5 trillion. The All-Share Index fell nearly 2% even as trading volumes and the number of deals rose.

stories.h: Naira slips to N1,348/$ as FX turnover drops below $101 million
stories.e: The naira weakened for a second straight session to close at N1,348 to the dollar, as interbank foreign-exchange turnover fell to about $101 million from roughly $119 million the previous day. Nairametrics noted the currency has now given back a significant share of the gains it made between July and September.

stories.h: Bank of Industry, IFC sign $50m loan deal to expand finance for Nigerian MSMEs
stories.e: The Bank of Industry and the International Finance Corporation have signed a $50 million loan agreement to widen financing access for Nigerian small and medium-sized enterprises, with at least a quarter of the funds reserved for women-owned businesses. The deal was announced at the Africa Financial Industry Summit in Luanda, Angola.

stories.h: Rising energy costs drain N820.7bn from NGX-listed industrial firms
stories.e: Industrial goods companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange spent roughly N820.7 billion on fuel and power in the first nine months of 2026, a 6.3 per cent rise year-on-year that is squeezing profit margins. Cement producers Dangote and BUA account for the bulk of that spending, reflecting continued reliance on self-generated power due to an unreliable national grid. Analysts warn manufacturers are struggling to pass these rising costs on to customers.

stories.h: NUPRC approves 595 well re-entries and 145 new drilling operations as rig count hits 100
stories.e: Nigeria's upstream petroleum regulator, the NUPRC, said it has approved 595 well re-entries and 145 new drilling operations, pushing the country's active rig count to 100 for the first time in years. The commission described the increase as evidence of renewed investor confidence in Nigeria's oil and gas sector following recent reforms. A higher rig count typically signals increased future production and could support government revenue projections tied to oil output.

stories.h: Why Nigeria's cassava output still fails to feed its factories
stories.e: Despite being the world's largest cassava producer, Nigeria's processors continue to face feedstock shortages, according to findings discussed at an industry roundtable. The gap is attributed to overstated national output figures, low farm yields, high harvesting and transport costs, and the marketing of cheaper derivatives as substitutes for genuine cassava starch. Industry voices say solving the supply, cost and demand problems together is essential to unlocking the crop's industrial potential.

stories.h: Indorama commits $261m to a fourth fertiliser production line in Nigeria
stories.e: Indorama has issued a letter of award to South Korea's Daewoo for a new $261 million ammonia-urea line at its Eleme complex near Port Harcourt, a project that would lift the company's installed Nigerian urea capacity by about a third. The expansion comes as Gulf shipping disruptions have pushed global urea prices to multi-year highs.

stories.h: Dangote Cement, BUA spend N797 billion in energy cost
stories.e: Nigeria's two largest cement makers, Dangote Cement and BUA Cement, spent a combined N797.1 billion on fuel and power in the first nine months of 2026, nearly 7% more than a year earlier, as both firms leaned on self-generated electricity to cope with a national grid that failed repeatedly during the year. BUA's energy bill rose more than 21%, far outpacing Dangote's smaller 2% increase.

stories.h: BUA Cement, Nigerian Breweries among firms quitting the national grid for private power
stories.e: Regulatory filings show BUA Cement, Nigerian Breweries and several other manufacturers and public institutions secured permits for nearly 55 megawatts of captive power generation in the first half of 2026, as repeated grid collapses push major electricity users to go it alone. The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria says its members' spending on alternative power rose more than 20% to over ₦1.3 trillion in 2025, and analysts warn the exodus of big customers could further strain the national grid's finances.

stories.h: Dangote Launches $2.5bn Fuel Storage and Pipeline Project in Namibia
stories.e: Aliko Dangote has broken ground on a $2.5 billion fuel storage and pipeline project near Namibia's Walvis Bay port, targeting landlocked southern African markets that rely on imported petroleum. The facility will include roughly four million barrels of storage capacity and is tied to a proposed 1,700-kilometre pipeline linking Namibia to Botswana and South Africa.

stories.h: Nigeria's biggest firms hit by fourfold surge in energy costs
stories.e: Nigeria's largest listed companies spent nearly four times more on energy in the first half of 2026 compared with a year earlier, driven by rising fuel prices. The surge adds pressure to manufacturers' already tight margins and raises fresh concerns about the cost of doing business in Nigeria's industrial sector.

stories.h: BUA Foods posts 11% profit growth despite falling revenue
stories.e: BUA Foods reported an 11% rise in nine-month profit to N450.47 billion even as revenue fell 19% to N1.15 trillion amid weaker consumer demand and lower prices. The company credited cost management and productivity gains for widening its profit margin despite softer sales.

stories.h: Dangote weighs up to $15bn refining and petrochemicals investment in Egypt
stories.e: Aliko Dangote is in talks with Egyptian officials over a potential $10-15 billion investment focused on oil refining and petrochemicals, aimed at turning Egypt from a fuel importer into a net exporter. The discussions followed a visit to Dangote's Lagos headquarters by Egypt's investment minister, and the final scale of the deal is still being negotiated.

stories.h: Beta Glass's nine-month profit falls 8% as finance costs and FX losses bite
stories.e: Packaging manufacturer Beta Glass saw after-tax profit slip 8.4% to N24.93 billion for the nine months to September, even though revenue rose nearly 5%, as finance costs jumped 45% and the company swung to a foreign-exchange loss. Nairametrics notes the company's third-quarter profit actually grew on its own, showing the annual decline was driven mainly by earlier-year pressures.

stories.h: Manufacturing credit falls 34% despite N4.65trn bank recapitalisation, economists warn
stories.e: New figures presented at a Lagos banking event show credit to Nigerian manufacturers has dropped by about a third since December 2024, even as lenders raised N4.65 trillion in fresh capital, with banks instead favouring oil and gas, trade and government securities. Economic analysts are calling for a coordinated financing framework, warning that industrial growth is being starved of credit despite stronger bank balance sheets.

stories.h: Nigeria's top cement makers post combined N1.71trn profit in nine months
stories.e: Nigeria's three major cement producers posted a combined 37.8% rise in nine-month profit to N1.71 trillion, driven largely by stronger margins and cost efficiencies rather than higher sales volumes. The results underline the sector's continued profitability even as high construction costs remain a strain on ordinary Nigerians.

stories.h: Manufacturers face fresh squeeze on rising diesel prices
stories.e: Nigerian manufacturers are facing renewed cost pressure as diesel prices climb again, squeezing already thin margins for firms that rely on generators amid unreliable grid electricity. Industry groups warn the latest increase could further erode the sector's competitiveness and slow production.

stories.h: Manufacturers spent ₦1.35trn on alternative power in 2025 as sector shed nearly 19,000 jobs
stories.e: Manufacturers Association of Nigeria data presented at an industry AGM shows local manufacturers spent an estimated ₦1.35 trillion on alternative power in 2025, a 23% jump from the prior year, while the sector lost 18,935 jobs in the first half of 2025 alone, nearly double the losses recorded a year earlier. The figures point to unreliable grid supply, with delivered power still far below estimated industrial demand despite rising installed capacity.

stories.h: MAN: manufacturers still borrowing at 30% despite bank recapitalisation
stories.e: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria says its members are still borrowing at around 30% interest even after banks completed a recapitalisation exercise meant to expand lending, with association president Ifeanyi Okoye contrasting this with Chinese manufacturers who can access credit as cheap as 3%. Speaking at the Nigerian Economic Summit, he said only token rate cuts have reached manufacturers, leaving them at a cost disadvantage against foreign competitors.

stories.h: Nigeria to begin mass production of military munitions within a year, says defence minister
stories.e: Defence Minister Christopher Musa told delegates at Nigeria first Africa International Defence Exhibition in Lagos that local production of defence hardware for domestic use and export to other African countries will start within a year. The head of the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria pledged to expand production capacity, with the event drawing officials from more than 20 African countries.

stories.h: Manufacturers cut forex demand by $1bn through local sourcing
stories.e: Nigerian manufacturers reduced their foreign exchange needs by roughly $1 billion in the first half of 2026 as more firms source raw materials locally instead of importing them, according to new industry data. The shift toward backward integration reflects a wider push by producers to cut costs amid ongoing currency pressures.

stories.h: Manufacturers Association to Launch Industrial Energy Cost Reduction Programme in November
stories.e: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria said it will roll out a new programme next month aimed at helping member companies cut their energy costs, which have become one of the biggest drags on local production. The initiative responds to years of complaints from manufacturers about high electricity tariffs and unreliable power supply squeezing already-thin margins. Details on specific cost-saving measures are expected to be unveiled closer to the launch date.

stories.h: $5bn Ajaokuta steel revival still stalled by power and supply problems
stories.e: A fresh push to revive the long-dormant, $5 billion Ajaokuta Steel Complex is running into the same obstacles that have stalled the plant for decades, including unreliable power supply and shortages of raw materials, according to BusinessDay. The report underscores how one of Nigeria's biggest unfinished public infrastructure investments remains far from generating the industrial jobs and output officials have long promised.

stories.h: Gunmen abduct graduate, three others in Ogun, demand N500m ransom
stories.e: Armed kidnappers seized a recent graduate and three other people in Ogun State and are demanding a N500 million ransom for their release. The abduction adds to a continuing wave of kidnapping-for-ransom incidents affecting south-western Nigeria.

stories.h: Thugs attack NDC supporters, disrupt Peter Obi's Lagos town hall
stories.e: Suspected thugs armed with cutlasses and clubs stormed a Nigeria Democratic Congress town hall for presidential candidate Peter Obi in Oregun, Ikeja, forcing attendees to flee before supporters repelled the attackers. The assault is the latest in a string of attacks on opposition political gatherings across several states in recent weeks, raising fresh concern over political violence ahead of 2027.

stories.h: Plateau lifts curfew in Barkin Ladi, Bokkos and Mangu
stories.e: Plateau State has lifted the dusk-to-dawn curfew it had imposed on Barkin Ladi, Bokkos and Mangu local government areas following a spate of deadly attacks. The restriction had curtailed residents' movement for weeks as authorities worked to restore security in the affected communities.

stories.h: Amnesty condemns attack on PDP candidate Pantamis convoy in Gombe
stories.e: Amnesty International has condemned an attack in which armed thugs blocked a highway with burning tyres and smashed vehicle windscreens in an attempt to stop PDP governorship candidate Isa Pantamis convoy from reaching Gombe. The rights group said preliminary findings point to possible links with the ruling APC and criticised the apparent absence of arrests, urging a thorough investigation.

stories.h: Press groups condemn remand of FIJ journalist Daniel Ojukwu
stories.e: Daniel Ojukwu, a reporter with the Foundation for Investigative Journalism, has been remanded in Kuje Correctional Centre for 21 days after being arraigned on cybercrime and defamation charges linked to his reporting on an official government office. Press freedom groups, including CPJ and the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism, have condemned the remand and called for his release, warning of a chilling effect on reporting ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.h: Bandits burn 12 family members to death in Zamfara attack
stories.e: Gunmen attacked Gidan Taba village in Maradun local government area of Zamfara State on Saturday night, setting fire to a room and killing 12 members of one family, according to residents and the local council chairman. Police put the toll at 11 dead, while seven other residents were reportedly abducted during the raid. The attack adds to a string of deadly banditry incidents that have continued to afflict communities across the state.

stories.h: Twelve members of one family killed in Zamfara bandit attack
stories.e: Suspected bandits set fire to a room sheltering a family in Gidan Taba village, Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State, killing twelve people including a father, his wives and young children, according to the council chairman. Local vigilantes repelled the attackers and rescued some captives, while police say security operatives are pursuing the perpetrators; other outlets have put the toll at eleven or thirteen.

stories.h: 'Don't bring your camera': Lagos street gangs extort filmmakers
stories.e: Al Jazeera reports that filmmakers, photographers and journalists working in Lagos face routine threats and extortion demands from street touts known as agberos, with one crew member stabbed during a dispute over payment in Ajah. Lagos State's Commissioner for Information says no one has authority to demand such payments and that police will handle complaints, but analysts warn the harassment is pushing productions off the streets and could lead journalists to under-report sensitive events.

stories.h: Filmmakers and journalists in Lagos describe rising extortion by street touts
stories.e: Filmmakers, photographers and journalists working in Lagos say they are increasingly being stopped by groups of touts, or agberos, demanding payment before they are allowed to keep filming in public, with several reporting threats, assaults and damage to equipment when they refused. A Lagos state government spokesperson said no one has the authority to demand money from people filming in public and that such cases would be referred to the police, though analysts warn the harassment is already raising production costs and discouraging coverage of sensitive stories.

stories.h: Bandits kill twelve, abduct residents in overnight Zamfara attack
stories.e: Armed bandits stormed Gidan Taba village in Maradun council area of Zamfara State on Saturday night, setting fire to a room where a family had taken refuge from an abduction attempt and killing twelve people. Several residents were reportedly taken away, though local vigilantes later secured some releases after a gun battle, and the community is appealing for stronger security in the area.

stories.h: Lagos police detain officer after stray bullet kills girl during gang clash
stories.e: An Assistant Superintendent of Police has been detained after allegedly firing a shot that killed a young girl, Omole Taiwo, and wounded another during an operation to break up a violent clash between two rival groups in Ajegunle, Lagos. The state police commissioner visited the bereaved family and pledged a thorough investigation, while the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department for further action.

stories.h: HURIWA urges DSS to probe possible political motive behind Southern Kaduna attacks
stories.e: The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria has asked the Department of State Services to investigate whether renewed killings and abductions in Southern Kaduna are linked to recent political developments, including the choice of a Southern Kaduna Christian as a governorship running mate for 2027. The group is also pressing President Tinubu and other security chiefs to treat the recurring attacks as a national security priority.

stories.h: Amnesty International condemns attack on Atiku's ADC campaign convoy in Kebbi
stories.e: Amnesty International has condemned a violent attack on a campaign convoy belonging to ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar in Kebbi State, in which armed gangs reportedly blocked roads, assaulted supporters with cutlasses and damaged vehicles and journalists' equipment. The rights group says the incident, coming days after a similar clash in Sokoto, fits a pattern of repression against opposition campaigners and has urged Nigerian authorities to investigate and prosecute those responsible.

stories.h: Lagos police officer detained after shooting kills one girl, injures another in Ajegunle
stories.e: A Lagos police officer has been disarmed and detained after his gunfire killed one girl and wounded another during an operation against clashing youth groups in the Nosamu area of Ajegunle on the night of 5 November. The victim, identified as Omole Taiwo, died at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital after being transferred from a general hospital, while police have not explained how the officer's weapon discharged. Commissioner of Police Tijani Fatai visited the bereaved family and promised a thorough investigation, saying no officer found culpable would be shielded.

stories.h: Bandits terrorise eight Taraba communities, residents say 10 of 15 captives freed
stories.e: Residents of eight communities in Karim-Lamido, Taraba State, say armed men have been raiding farms, looting shops and sexually assaulting women for weeks, warning villagers against reporting attacks to security agencies. A community leader said 10 of 15 people abducted in recent raids have been released, while two more farmers were attacked near the Taraba-Plateau border days later; police said they had no record of the incidents at the time of reporting, highlighting a gap between community accounts and official response in Nigeria's rural security crisis.

stories.h: Troops Rescue 16 Kidnap Victims, Recover Weapons in Niger State Raid
stories.e: Nigerian Army troops freed 16 kidnapping victims and recovered rifles, rocket-propelled bombs, dozens of motorcycles and cash during a raid on suspected terrorists in Kontagora, Niger State. The rescue comes amid a wave of abductions in the state, including the kidnapping of 14 schoolchildren and a teacher days earlier, underscoring the continuing human cost of banditry in the region.

stories.h: IPOB Demands Release of Igbos It Says Are Unlawfully Detained
stories.e: The proscribed separatist group IPOB is demanding the release of dozens of Igbo detainees it says are being held unlawfully, after four suspected members were freed following four years in state security custody. The group says its lawyers have tracked 83 people moved from military detention in Kainji to prisons in Kuje, Keffi and Suleja, and is calling on the UN, US and EU to intervene.

stories.h: Abducted Plateau varsity student freed
stories.e: A 100-level Plateau State University student abducted from an off-campus residence near Bokkos was freed after her captors fled when a joint university-military team closed in, according to school and security officials. She was taken to hospital for treatment, and no arrests had been reported as of the latest update.

stories.h: Police react to viral video on alleged officers' brutality in Osun
stories.e: Nigerian police responded after a video alleging brutality by officers in Osun State circulated widely online and drew public outcry. The force's reaction comes amid continuing scrutiny of police conduct in the state, where similar allegations have previously triggered disciplinary action.

stories.h: Group calls for withdrawal of charges against Kaduna journalist
stories.e: The rights group LEDAP is calling for charges to be dropped against 23-year-old Kaduna radio reporter Farida Isiak, who was prosecuted over a Facebook post criticising police and was briefly convicted by a Sharia court before the ruling was set aside. The group says her parents were also detained, and is demanding an independent probe into what it calls a conflict-of-interest investigation led by the officer she had criticised.

stories.h: Nigeria and EU sign deal to facilitate return of irregular migrants
stories.e: Nigeria and the European Union have signed an agreement intended to make it easier to return Nigerians living in Europe without valid immigration status. The deal forms part of broader migration cooperation between Abuja and Brussels.

stories.h: Nigeria fields third-largest delegation among nations at COP31 climate summit
stories.e: Nigeria sent the third-largest national delegation to the COP31 climate summit, a record gathering that is drawing global attention to Africa's role in climate negotiations. The scale of Nigeria's presence reflects the country's push to secure climate financing and shape outcomes relevant to Africa, including adaptation funding and the energy transition. Separately at the summit, African youth delegates presented a mapping of water challenges across 51 countries, calling for a greater role in policy decisions.

stories.h: AfDB and AFD sign five-year deal to expand African infrastructure financing
stories.e: The African Development Bank Group and France's Agence Francaise de Developpement signed a memorandum of understanding on the sidelines of the Paris Peace Forum, extending their partnership on jointly financed infrastructure projects across 14 African countries, including Nigeria, through 2031. The deal covers energy, transport, water, agriculture and digital infrastructure, building on 17 projects the two institutions have already co-financed since 2021.

stories.h: Nigeria pitches $2.2bn flare gas capture plan to investors at COP31
stories.e: At a side event at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission chief executive Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan pitched a $2.2 billion flare gas capture programme to international investors, aimed at ending routine gas flaring at Nigerian oil fields. The event also launched a new emissions-tracking portal, even as official data show the share of gas flared in Nigeria rose in August to its highest level since October 2025.

stories.h: Amnesty says UN and South Sudan officials failed to stop village massacre
stories.e: Amnesty International has accused United Nations and South Sudanese officials of failing to act on warnings that could have prevented a deadly massacre in a South Sudanese village. The finding adds to mounting criticism of the international communitys response to recurring violence in the country.

stories.h: COP31 climate talks open in Antalya amid finance dispute and calls to get serious
stories.e: The COP31 United Nations climate conference opened in Antalya, Turkey, with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urging world leaders to get serious about cutting emissions. The ceremony was delayed by around ninety minutes amid a dispute over whether climate finance would feature on the formal agenda, a standoff that was eventually resolved partly in favour of developing countries. The outcome will be closely watched by African and other Global South delegations seeking stronger commitments on climate finance.

stories.h: African nations to press for climate finance commitments at COP31
stories.e: Negotiators representing Africas 54 nations say they will push for predictable, grant-based climate finance and a full replenishment of the Green Climate Fund when COP31 opens in Antalya, Turkiye. The African Group of Negotiators, which includes Nigerias delegation, insists wealthier nations must meet their existing Paris Agreement obligations before any new financing contributors are brought in, and wants a broader, more equitable approach to the global shift away from fossil fuels.

stories.h: WHO: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak is now the largest ever recorded there
stories.e: The World Health Organisation says the Ebola outbreak centred on Ituri and North Kivu provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the largest the country has ever recorded, with over 10,600 confirmed cases and more than 5,100 deaths as of early November. Nigeria is among five countries to have recorded a case, after a patient diagnosed in Abuja in October was evacuated to Switzerland for treatment.

stories.h: WHO backs trials of two new vaccines against DRC's deadly Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
stories.e: The World Health Organization's vaccine advisory group has recommended two additional candidate vaccines, Oxford/Serum Institute's ChAdOx1 and Moderna's mRNA-1469, for testing against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola during the Democratic Republic of Congo's ongoing outbreak. It marks the first time vaccines designed specifically for this Ebola strain have been trialled during an active outbreak, with results expected in early 2027. The WHO has also urged countries not to impose travel restrictions on people from the DRC in response to the outbreak.

stories.h: US lawmaker who accused USAID of funding Boko Haram loses re-election bid
stories.e: Pennsylvania Republican Scott Perry, who in 2025 told Congress without evidence that USAID had funnelled money to Boko Haram and other terrorist groups, lost his House seat in the November 3 midterms to Democrat Janelle Stelson. Nigerian officials and a Nigerian lawyer had previously pushed back on the unsubstantiated claim, which a former US ambassador to Nigeria also rejected.

stories.h: 14 Nigerian-Americans win state and local races in US midterm elections
stories.e: Abike Dabiri-Erewa, chair of Nigeria's diaspora commission, says 14 Nigerian-Americans won seats across the United States in Tuesday's midterms, including state legislature wins in Georgia, Texas, Ohio, Minnesota and Michigan, plus Will Jawando's election as Montgomery County executive in Maryland. The wins add to a growing number of Nigerian-Americans holding elected office across multiple US states.

stories.h: World Bank raises alarm as developing countries' external debt hits record $9.4 trillion
stories.e: The World Bank's newly released International Debt Report found that developing countries' external debt hit a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, growing at its fastest pace since 2021 as governments leaned more heavily on private creditors and bond markets. The report singles out Nigeria, noting its external debt stock climbed to $54.52 billion by mid-2026 and that the country spent $5.21 billion servicing external debt last year.

stories.h: Nigerian-born scholar Dapo Akande elected judge of the International Court of Justice
stories.e: Dapo Akande, a Nigerian-born Oxford professor of international law running as the United Kingdom's candidate, has been elected to a nine-year term on the International Court of Justice, the UN's top judicial body. He will take his seat on the Hague-based court in February 2027. His election highlights the continued influence of Nigerian-trained legal scholars within major international institutions.

stories.h: Mo Ibrahim warns Africa is backsliding into a 'strongman' era
stories.e: Sudanese-British billionaire Mo Ibrahim says the continent's governance gains have stalled and that authoritarian 'strongmen' are resurging, tying the trend to a broader global drift away from democratic norms. He pointed to his foundation's governance index, which he says shows little improvement across much of Africa in recent years, as a warning sign for citizens and policymakers alike.

stories.h: Nigeria, Russia agree to renegotiate 59-year-old aviation pact
stories.e: Nigeria's aviation minister Festus Keyamo met Russian officials at the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow and agreed to renegotiate the countries' 1967 bilateral air services agreement, with both sides aiming to finalise a new deal in Saint Petersburg by April 2027. Neither side has yet disclosed what routes or airlines the updated agreement would cover.

stories.h: Nigeria, Russia agree to replace 59-year-old aviation agreement
stories.e: Nigeria's aviation minister Festus Keyamo and Russian officials agreed, on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, to renegotiate the countries' 1967 air services pact. Both sides have set up negotiating teams and aim to sign a replacement agreement in Saint Petersburg in April 2027, though no route or airline details have been disclosed yet.

stories.h: CAR tightens border checks as DR Congo Ebola cases rise
stories.e: The Central African Republic has tightened checks at its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as an Ebola outbreak there continues to spread into new provinces. The heightened screening aims to prevent cross-border transmission as regional health authorities scale up containment efforts.

stories.h: Russian drone strike kills 14 at Ukraine train station
stories.e: A Russian drone strike on a train station in Ukraine has killed 14 people, in what officials described as a horrific attack on civilian infrastructure. The strike adds to the mounting civilian toll of Russia's continuing war against Ukraine.

stories.h: Nigeria joins 129 other nations at UN in demanding end to US embargo on Cuba
stories.e: Nigeria was among 130 countries that backed a UN General Assembly resolution calling for an end to the decades-old US economic embargo on Cuba, a vote the US and Israel opposed and 25 nations abstained from. Most African states supported the resolution, which has passed annually since 1992 and comes as fresh US sanctions have deepened Cuba's economic strain.

stories.h: Nigeria downgrades delegation to Russia-Africa summit, keeps Tinubu and VP away
stories.e: Nigeria sent only Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Sola Enikanolaiye to the two-day Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, after earlier plans for Vice President Kashim Shettima to lead the delegation were quietly dropped without explanation from the presidency. Analysts link the low-key presence to Nigeria's deepening ties with the United States and the approaching 2027 election campaign.

stories.h: Flamingos' Umejiaku says FIFA U-17 World Cup best player award was a first
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos midfielder Oluebube Umejiaku said winning the best player award at the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup was the first individual honour of her career. The award adds to a strong showing by Nigeria's youth teams on the global stage this year.

stories.h: Super Eagles seek redemption against Tanzania in Uyo AFCON qualifier
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles face Tanzania in Uyo in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, looking to bounce back after their recent defeat to Guinea-Bissau. Coach Eric Chelle said the team is focused solely on securing victory to keep their qualification hopes on track.

stories.h: Tinubu rewards Flamingos with ₦100m savings bonds each after historic World Cup win
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu approved a ₦100 million federal savings bond for every member of the Flamingos, Nigeria's under-17 women's team, after they became the first African side to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup. Head coach Busari Hakeem Ishola will receive ₦100 million in cash, while other technical staff get ₦50 million each. The team beat Japan 2-1 in the final after recovering from an opening defeat to Poland, winning six matches in a row to lift the trophy.

stories.h: Super Eagles full 24-man squad assembles in Uyo for Tanzania qualifier
stories.e: All 24 invited Super Eagles players, including Alex Iwobi, Ademola Lookman and Wilfred Ndidi, have arrived in camp in Uyo ahead of a must-win 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Tanzania. The early assembly is intended to give the coaching staff extra time to work on tactics and match fitness before Fridays game.

stories.h: Flamingos crowned world champions, return home to Abuja reception
stories.e: Nigeria's under-17 women's football team, the Flamingos, arrived back in Abuja to a warm reception after being crowned world champions, having beaten Japan 2-1 in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco. The victory marks Nigeria's first title at this level, surpassing the squad's previous best finish of third place.

stories.h: Nwankwo and Bright win Nigeria's first two golds at Dakar Youth Olympics
stories.e: Rosemary Nwankwo and Gift Bright won Nigeria's first two gold medals at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, taking the girls' and boys' 100m sprint titles respectively. Bright's personal-best run made him the first Nigerian to win the boys' 100m crown at the Youth Olympics, lifting the country to joint 14th on the medal table alongside Ecuador as the Games continue in Senegal.

stories.h: Flamingos become first African side to win FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 in Rabat, Morocco, to become the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, with midfielder Oluebube Umejiaku named the tournament's best player. President Bola Tinubu congratulated the squad and coaching staff, calling the victory a source of pride for the country, as the team's run through the tournament drew widespread celebration across Nigeria.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos beat Japan to win first-ever FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos defeated Japan 2-1 in Rabat, Morocco to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, becoming the first African team ever to claim the title. Goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku secured the win after the side recovered from an opening defeat to Poland to post six consecutive victories through the knockout rounds.

stories.h: Flamingos make history, beat Japan to win Nigerias first U-17 Womens World Cup
stories.e: Nigerias Flamingos defeated Japan to claim the countrys first-ever FIFA U-17 Womens World Cup title, a landmark achievement for Nigerian womens football celebrated by officials and fans nationwide. Senate President Godswill Akpabio and other public figures congratulated the team, with coach Fatai Busari crediting the win to years of sustained development work rather than a one-off success.

stories.h: Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win Nigeria's first FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's football team, the Flamingos, defeated Japan 2-1 in Morocco to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final, becoming the first African side to lift the trophy. Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scored for Nigeria, with Fuki Ito replying for Japan, capping a run in which the Flamingos recovered from an opening defeat to Poland to win five successive matches.

stories.h: Flamingos chase Nigeria's first FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title against Japan
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos face Japan in Rabat on Saturday evening, seeking a historic first FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title after beating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-final to reach their first-ever final. Japan reached the final by edging North Korea 4-1 on penalties after a 1-1 draw. A Nigerian win would make it the first African country to hold FIFA titles in both the men's and women's U-17 categories.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos face Japan in U-17 Women's World Cup final, chasing Africa's first title
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team has won five straight matches in Morocco to reach the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final against Japan, including a 3-1 semi-final win over Brazil. A victory on Saturday would make Nigeria the first African nation to win the tournament, against a Japanese side chasing its second title in four final appearances.

stories.h: South Africa Leads After Day One of 2026 All Africa Challenge Trophy in Abuja
stories.e: South Africa tops the team standings after the opening round of the 2026 All Africa Challenge Trophy, a continental women's golf championship Nigeria is hosting in Abuja, with Kenya and Tanzania close behind. Host nation Nigeria sits in fifth as the tournament, which draws teams from across the continent, continues through the week.

stories.h: Cristiano Ronaldo Retires From Portugal National Team
stories.e: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football after 23 years representing Portugal, closing out a career that spanned six World Cups and the men's all-time international scoring record. The decision followed a fallout with new national coach Jorge Jesus, who had benched the veteran forward and signalled he would not start him going forward.

stories.h: Flamingos beat Brazil to reach FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's football team, the Flamingos, beat Brazil in the semi-final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco to reach the tournament final, drawing congratulatory messages from President Tinubu and other officials. The result extends a strong run by the junior team and has drawn widespread celebration nationwide ahead of the final.

stories.h: Flamingos beat Brazil 3-1 to reach first-ever U-17 Women's World Cup final
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 girls' team, the Flamingos, defeated Brazil 3-1 in Rabat to reach their first-ever FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final, with Queen Joseph opening the scoring before Awawu Bashiru added a late brace. The milestone result sets up a title clash against Japan on Saturday.

stories.h: One player killed, several injured in road accident involving Nigerian girls' football academy
stories.e: A player with the Ayisat Yusuf Football Academy died and several teammates were injured when their team's vehicle was involved in a road accident while travelling from Ogun State to a league fixture in Lagos. The academy's founder confirmed the death but has not released further details on how the crash occurred. The team's driver also sustained serious injuries, with some players reportedly requiring urgent medical care.

stories.h: Flamingos reach first-ever U-17 Women's World Cup final after facing Brazil in semis
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos took on Brazil in Rabat for a place in Saturday's FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final, a stage the team has never reached before in the tournament's history. The match drew heavy attention from Nigerian sports fans hoping to see the junior women's team deliver a rare global trophy run. A win would mark a milestone for Nigerian women's football development at the youth level.

stories.h: Tinubu Fulfils $100,000 Cash Promise to Super Falcons After WAFCON Win
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu's promised $100,000 cash reward to each member of the Super Falcons for their WAFCON title victory has now been paid out, months after the pledge was first announced. The payout, alongside earlier national honours and housing pledges, had previously drawn public debate over the scale of rewards for athletes compared with other national priorities.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos reach U-17 Women's World Cup semi-final
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos defeated Venezuela 1-0 in a tense quarter-final at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, with captain Azeezat Oduntan converting a late penalty in the 89th minute. The win sends Nigeria to the semi-finals for only the second time in the tournament's history.
